question: Which of the following metals is susceptible to fire if kept in the open?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Potassium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Potassium is a chemical element with the atomic number 19 and the **symbol K**.
 
• It is extremely reactive and reacts with air as well as water vigorously due to these characteristics they are easily susceptible to fire when kept in open.
 
• Potassium is a silvery-white metal that can be cut with a knife with little effort. 
 
• They have low melting points and low densities
 
• In the periodic table, potassium is an alkali metal, which all have a single valence electron in the outer electron shell.
 
• In nature, Potassium occurs only in ionic salts.
 
• Uses of potassium:
 
 
• It is used as a heat exchange medium and in nuclear power plants.
 
• Potassium salts are a component of fertiliser.
 
• It is one of the most important nutrients for the human body.
 
• Potash can be used to make glass, soap, and a variety of other products.
